tossups.text: Buchholz and MacDougall named one type of these figures whose side lengths and area are all rational numbers after David P. Robbins. Carlyle circles can be used to construct one of these shapes. A regular one of these shapes is the shape with the lowest number of sides that cannot tile a plane. An icosahedron has 20 hexagonal sides and twelve sides made up of these shapes. The exterior angles of this shape are 72 degrees each, and its interior angles sum to 540. For 10 points, name this five-sided polygon.

In one novel by this author, the protagonist searches for his lost sister for 777 years, 7 months, 7 days after drinking a magic beverage. In that novel, this author created a character whom Virgil Jones guides to the mythical Calf Island, whose inhabitants are immortal. In another novel, this author created a protagonist who mistakes a phantasm called "Nobodaddy" for his father before dying at the hands of the Old Man of the River, coming back to life, and realizing that the world is like a video game with levels and lives. In that novel, this author wrote of the Khalifas, the youngest of whom is the title character, who seeks out the title substance, guarded by The Aalim. This author's first novel centers on Axona Indian Flapping Eagle, who searches for his sister Bird-Dog. The author of Luka and the Fire of Life and Grimus, FTP, name this man who also wrote The Ground Beneath Her Feet and penned a novel about Saleem Sinai as well as one that inspired the Ayatollah to issue a fatwa.

This province became a colony shortly after the 1858 Fraser Canyon Gold Rush. Over a thousand residents of the Downtown Eastside neighborhood were evicted before this province's Expo 86. This province, the sixth to join confederation, developed its fur-trading posts into the cities of Kamloops and Nanaimo (nah-NAI-moh). This province's Kwakiutl (KWAH-kee-oo-tul) and Tsimshian (SIM-shee-an) peoples faced discrimination during the development of a city that later hosted the 2010 Winter Olympics. An 18th-century British explorer names, for 10 points, what province's city of Vancouver?

The van der Waals equation corrects this quantity using the parameter "b." Isochoric processes perform no work because it remains constant. Kinetic theory assumes that this quantity is zero for single molecules. Boyle's law states it has an inverse relation with pressure, which is multiplied by this quantity in the ideal gas law. For 10 points, name this quantity that is constant for solids and liquids but variable for gases and is often measured in liters.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for immunodeficiency. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this vaccine-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The vaccine is a key component of the Immune system, involved in immunodeficiency.

tossups.text: Many of this artist's works, including "plein air"[plen ayr]paintings of the Rouen Cathedral and ofhis wife, Camille, on her deathbed, are held in the Musee d'Orsay. This artist painted numerous views of the English houses of Parliament and of his garden in Giverny,which held an arched, Japanese-style green bridge over a pond of flowers. For ten points, name this French artist who painted many images ofWaterliliesas aleader of the Impressionist movement.

The protagonist of this novel learns that one character is a printer named Gerard Duval after finding his wallet. In one scene in this novel, three characters swim naked across a canal carrying only boots full of food. Earlier, the main character is attacked by a bull mastiff when he and Kat steal a goose. This novel's brief final section features an abrupt shift to the third person, and earlier in this novel, Mueller takes a pair of boots from the dying Himmerich. The protagonist of this novel helps beat up Himmelstoss, the drill sergeant who trained Paul Baumer's squad before it was sent to the trenches. For 10 points, name this World War I novel by Erich Maria Remarque.
tossups.answer: All Quiet on the Western Front
acceptableAnswers: All Quiet on the Western Front
The All Quiet on the Western Front

tossups.text: Hesiod describes the collective voice of this group with the word ossa. The name of a member of this group was given to an aspect of Aphrodite that was considered to oppose her "Pandemos" aspect. Many writers describe this group hanging out in the Vale of Tempe. Members of this group turned the daughters of Pierus into birds after winning a singing contest against them, though they themselves were sometimes called Pierides [pee-AIR-uh-dees]. They were believed by many to live in the Corycian cave, and thus were called "Corycian nymphs." This group was born of the union of Zeus and a Titaness who personified memory, Mnemosyne [nuh-MAH-zin-ee]. For 10 points, Calliope [kuh-LIE-oh-pee] and Clio are among what nine goddesses of inspiration and the arts?

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for major arteries (aorta, carotid, femoral). It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this aorta-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The aorta is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in major arteries (aorta, carotid, femoral).

tossups.text: This ruler had Serapios, the strategos of Cypros, killed and this ruler was forced into exile by the eunuch Pothinus. This ruler's sister Arsinoe IV was scandalously murdered on the steps of the Temple of Ephesus. This ruler allegedly won a bet by drinking pearls dissolved in vinegar, and while besieged by enemies, this monarch asked for and received a basket of figs. This ruler snuck into a room hidden inside a rolled-up carpet, and after she and her lover were defeated at the Battle of Actium, this woman killed herself with an asp. For 10 points, name this last Ptolemaic pharaoh of Egypt, the lover of Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.

Robert Dahl argued against this work's central point in a study of New Haven. One chapter of this work claims that the New Deal was the fourth epoch of the title entity, and that currently it is in the fifth. This work asserts that there is no such thing as a self-made man in a section about how corrupt institutions lead to a "higher immorality." Its author refers to a certain group as "the warlords"; they are among those whom this work claims work in "The Conservative Mood." Other chapters of this work describe "The Political Directorate," "The Chief Executives," and "The Corporate Rich," all of whom are part of the title group. For 10 points, name this book which claims that a small social group controlling financial, military, and political interests controls America, a work of C. Wright Mills.

This psychologist extended the capacity model of attention to allow for a flexible capacity, which can be divided to an extent determined by effort. This living man showed that individuals underestimate the amount of time they need to do any task, which is the "planning fallacy." This author of Attention and Effort wrote that people are more likely to identify Linda as a "bank teller and feminist" than just a "bank teller." This man formulated the concept of "anchoring," and he identified availability and representativeness as examples of heuristics that lead to biases. This Nobel laureate proposed that utility be modeled as a function of change in wealth instead of absolute wealth, which helps explain why people avoid risk. For 10 points, name this co-developer of prospect theory with Amos Tversky.

This element's concentration is measured with the Clark electrode. Preston Cloud used banded iron formations to date a high concentration of this element to 2.4 billion years ago. A bond between atoms of this element is broken in the Chapman cycle. A decrease in this element's concentration occurs during eutrophication from algal blooms. By mass, this is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust. The Montreal Protocol banned CFCs to mitigate how a compound of this element was depleted over the South Pole, leading to the formation of a namesake "hole" of that compound. For 10 points, name this element that makes up ozone and about 21% of the atmosphere with nitrogen.

This composer's Five Variants of Dives and Lazarus, scored for harp and string orchestra, is based on one of the folk tunes he quoted in his English Folk Song Suite. This composer's first and longest symphony has a slow movement titled "On the Beach at Night, Alone," which makes use of a baritone and chorus. This composer scored a work for an expanded string orchestra divided into three parts - an orchestra, a smaller 9-player group, and a string quartet - which is based on the Renaissance melody "Why fum'th ("FYOOM-ith") in fight." For 10 points, name this British composer of A Sea Symphony, Fantasia on a Theme by Thomas Tallis, and The Lark Ascending.

One conflict for independence within this nation was known as the Little War, which took place shortly after the Pact of Zanjon ended the Ten Years' War. One leader of this nation led the 26th of July Movement that overthrew Fulgencio Batista, and U.S. control over this nation was the subject of the Teller Amendment. The best known leader of this nation was the target of the Bay of Pigs invasion, and this country was blockaded by the U.S. during a namesake "missile crisis." For 10 points, name this Caribbean nation long ruled by Fidel Castro.

This figure appears between the goddesses Liberty and Victory in a ceiling fresco depicting their apotheosis by Constantino Brumidi. Gilbert Stuart's Lansdowne Portrait, which depicts this figure, was legendarily saved from the burning White House by Dolley Madison. This title figure of Emmanuel Leutze's ["loyt-zuh's"] most famous painting stands as a billowing, historically inaccurate flag is held by James Monroe in a boat traveling across the Delaware River. For 10 points, name this leader depicted on the one-dollar bill, the first U.S. President.

This man defeated Isaac Dukas at the castle of Kantaras, and several months earlier, he attacked the city of Messina in order to secure the release of his sister Joan from King Tancred of Sicily, but that attack also incited this man's brother into rebellion. While traveling through Vienna in disguise he was captured and imprisoned at the behest of Duke Leopold, and he died while attacking the castle of Chalus after a dispute over a gold deposit. With the help of Philip Augustus, this man captured Acre, but after failing to capture Jerusalem, he agreed to a three-year truce with Saladin, ending the Third Crusade. For 10 points, name this English king and brother of John Lackland, nicknamed for his courage.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for larynx and vocal cords. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this pharynx-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The pharynx is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in larynx and vocal cords.

tossups.text: One character in this novel botches an operation on Hypolite's broken leg once his first wife, Heloise, dies. Monsieur Homais is a pharmacist in this novel who undermines the reputation of the protagonist's husband, Charles, in the town of Yonville. The title character of this novel has affairs with Rodolphe Boulanger and Leon Dupuis while accruing an enormous debt, which leads to her suicide via arsenic. For 10 points, name this novel about a French doctor's wife by Gustave Flaubert.

The victorious commander set out from Fort William and benefited from the rain which made the opposition's fifty-three French artillery pieces ineffective. The smaller force hid behind a hill near the Hooghli River and was aided by an agreement with Mir Jaffar, who remained neutral. Thus, the Nawab of Bengal had no reinforcements and Robert Clive's forces were victorious. For 10 points, identify this June 1757 battle that secured British dominance in India.

parts.text: Name this organelle that packages cellular materials into vesicles. It is named for an Italian scientist.
Leigh's syndrome is a lethal disease that affects the maternally inherited DNA of this organelle. It is known as the "powerhouse of the cell."
Another mitochondrial disease, Pearson syndrome, can cause failure of this organ by affecting alpha and beta cells.

bonuses.leadin: Achondrogenesis, a disease that affects bone and cartilage development, is a disease of this organelle. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this play. Juan Julian is shot in this play as he reads, in Spanish, the line "what logic can there be in killing a man to regain harmony with a woman..." as part of his job as a lector in a cigar factory.
Anna in the Tropics is by Nilo Cruz, an author of this ethnicity. Cesar and Nestor Castillo perform on I Love Lucy in a novel by Oscar Hijuelos, another author of this ethnicity.
In Anna in the Tropics, the lector Juan Julian reads the cigar factory workers Anna Karenina, a novel by this Russian author of War and Peace.

bonuses.leadin: In this play, Santiago tells his wife that he sees "a line of little ants carrying breadcrumbs on their backs," but the crumbs they are taking are his "dignity." For 10 points each:

parts.text: The fourth-largest island in the world, this nation, with capital at Antananarivo, is noted for its immense biodiversity, with the ring-tailed lemur being the most prominent of its endemic species.

A former possession of the Sultanate of Oman, this largely Muslim, semi-autonomous island group lies off the coast of mainland Tanzania and is the birthplace of Freddie Mercury of the classic rock group Queen.

The population of this archipelago nation, the smallest in Africa, largely speaks a French creole language despite being a colony of the United Kingdom until 1976. It lies northeast of Madagascar, and its capital is Victoria.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name some African islands of the Indian Ocean.

parts.text: Name this 3-D shape that has six square faces.
A cube contains eight of these 3-D corners, where three or more edges meet. The Euler ["OY-ler"] characteristic equals the number of these things, minus the number of edges, plus the number of faces.
The cube is a member of this group of five polyhedra, which also include the tetrahedron and the dodecahedron. Their namesake Greek philosopher described them in their Timaeus.

bonuses.leadin: The tesseract is the four-dimensional analogue of this shape. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with metabolism regulation.
What is the main function of the thyroid in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to metabolism regulation.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: Name this Scottish economist who built on the ideas of the French physiocrats in his The Wealth of Nations.
Smith used this two-word phrase to describe the tendency of markets to self-correct. In The Wealth of Nations, he says that this leads one to "promote an end which was no part of his intention".
Smith's works laid the foundation for this kind of economy, especially its laissez-faire kind. It is based on private ownership, in contrast to communism.

bonuses.leadin: This man described a hypothetical pin factory in his best-known work. For 10 points each:

parts.text: One Frost poem states that "ice-storms" bend these trees to stay, and ends by stating "One could do worse than be a swinger of" these trees.
In this Frost poem, the narrator states of his neighbor that "He is all pine and I am apple orchard." The narrator's neighbor repeats the proverb "Good fences make good neighbors" in this poem.
This Frost poem describes the death of a boy whose hand was cut off by a buzzsaw, and takes its title from a line in Macbeth.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following about Robert Frost poems, for 10 points each.

parts.text: This Norse goddess had a chariot pulled by two cats. It was customary to give cats to newlyweds to represent this goddess' blessings on the couple.
Freyja was not the only Norse deity to have a chariot pulled by unconventional animals: Thor's chariot was pulled by two of these animals, named Tanngrisnir and Tanngnjostr ("tong-nyo-ster").
In addition to his ravens Huginn and Muninn and the horse Sleipnir, Odin had two of these animals, named Geri and Freki.

bonuses.leadin: Animals play many roles in Norse mythology, from harbingers of doom to general annoyances. For ten points each, answer the following questions about the fylgja ("fill-juh"), or animal companions, of the gods.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with carbon dioxide transport.
What is the main function of the diffusion in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to carbon dioxide transport.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human respiratory system.

parts.text: Name this prominent Republican politician who, as Secretary of State under President Andrew, purchased Alaska from Russia in 1867.
With the assistance of political boss Thurlow Weed, Seward served as Governor and Senator of this state, where he was forced to deploy the militia at its capital, Albany.
One of the reasons Seward lost the 1860 Republican nomination to Abraham Lincoln was the opposition of this man, the editor of the New York Tribune.

bonuses.leadin: In one speech, this political figure infuriated slaveowners by calling on a "higher law" than the Constitution, for 10 points:

parts.text: This son of Sven Forkbeard chased Edmund across the countryside for several years before forcing him to partition the Kingdom. Edmund's subsequent death, possibly caused by "accidentally" sitting on a Viking sword several dozen times, left England completely under the control of this Danish king.

Much of Edmund's trouble came thanks to the persistent incompetence of this man, his father. This king, whose epithet denotes his lack of prudent counsel, succeeded his murdered brother Edward the Martyr and triggered Danish wrath by ordering the ethnic Danes in England slaughtered on St. Brice's Day for no particular reason.

Edmund's subjugation by Canute concluded at this 1016 battle, which saw Danish forces led by Canute and Thorkell the Tall massacre English troops, who were betrayed by Eadric Streona. Eadric was reportedly so eager to betray his allies that he mistook a soldier for Edmund, beheaded him, and paraded the head around for an hour before realizing his error.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following sources of frustration for Edmund Ironside, for 10 points each.

parts.text: The Rostow and Gerschenkron models were opposed by dependency theory in the controversy over what process of economic growth in countries that start as relatively poor?

The third stage of the Rostow model, when economic growth dramatically increases, is known by this term. Its preconditions include investment of over 10% of national income, a growing manufacturing sector, and the creation of social and political institutions which allow for productive economic activity.

Rostow's model heavily influenced the institution-based investment in Latin America promoted in the 1960s by this program, which the Kennedy administration appointed Teodoro Moscoso to lead after the 1961 Punta del Este Conference.

bonuses.leadin: In the 1960s, this process was believed to follow a fixed sequence of steps described in a book subtitled "A Non-Communist Manifesto." For 10 points each:

parts.text: What proteins, also called immunoglobulins, are produced by plasma cells as part of the immune response?
Antibodies found in this disease include anti-CCP antibodies and this disease's namesake factor. This autoimmune disease mostly affects the joints.
In RA, the protein DKK-1 is overexpressed, causing inhibition of these signaling pathways. They are named for a family of proteins that bind to Frizzled receptors and activate beta-catenin.

bonuses.leadin: The cells that make these proteins can undergo isotype switching to change part of their heavy chains, for example switching from IgM to IgG. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Baroque-era description of the life of Jesus.
Another important liturgical work by the composer of the St. Matthew Passion is this compendious 27-movement mass, his only complete setting of the Ordinary.
This man wrote the St. Matthew Passion and Mass in B Minor, as well as The Well-Tempered Clavier and The Art of the Fugue.

bonuses.leadin: A young Felix Mendelssohn conducted this piece in 1829, leading to a revival of its composer's works. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this teacher who agreed to stand trial for teaching evolution in violation of Tennessee's Butler Act in hopes of having the act struck down.
This devout Christian, who advocated free silver in the "Cross of Gold" speech, became the most famous of Scopes's prosecutors, allowing Clarence Darrow to cross-examine him.
Bryan lost the 1896 Presidential election after being heavily outspent by this man. He was succeeded by Theodore Roosevelt after his 1901 assassination in Buffalo, New York.

bonuses.leadin: In 1925, this high school teacher in Dayton, Tennessee agreed to be prosecuted for a crime which, in his memory, he never actually committed. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This Italian sculpted a horned Moses and painted Adam touching the finger of God on the Sistine Chapel ceiling.
This sculpture by Michelangelo depicts a legendary Jewish king standing casually with his slingshot over his shoulder, as he prepares to slay the giant Goliath.
This other Michelangelo sculpture shows a young Virgin Mary cradling the adult corpse of Jesus as if she were holding her infant child.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, identify an artist and his works.

parts.text: Name this 1954 battle in which the French were defeated by communist troops under Vo Nguyen Giap.
The Battle of Dien Bien Phu took place in this modern day country, which was later split into North and South fragments and reunified after a lengthy American military intervention.
This 1954 conference, begun while the Battle of Dien Bien Phu was still raging, ended the First Indochina War and formally recognized North and South Vietnam as separate states.

bonuses.leadin: One leader of this battle compared the opposing position to the bottom of a rice bowl. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with stomach anatomy.
What is the main function of the esophagus in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to stomach anatomy.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Name this legendary story in which a schoolteacher named Ichabod Crane unsuccessfully fends off Brom Bones.
This antagonist is a Hessian who fought at a battle in the Revolutionary War. This spectre is generally considered to be Brom Bones in disguise.
Washington Irving published the stories "Rip Van Winkle" and "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow" in The Sketch Book of this pseudonym.

bonuses.leadin: The protagonist of this short story tries to win Katrina von Tassel's heart. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This Macedonian-born viceroy and father of ninety-five children killed the last Mamluks and achieved de facto independence for Egypt by the 1830s.
This 1827 battle, often called the last major clash between wooden ships, was the turning point for victory by the allies of Greek independence over the Ottomans.
This 1878 treaty, which ended the Russo-Turkish War and was softened at the Berlin Congress, recognized the independenece of Serbia, Montenegro, Romania, and Bulgaria.

bonuses.leadin: The Ottoman Empire rapidly lost territory in the nineteenth century. For 10 points each:
